nodes.label: Frame 02101: Daytime Colour Overhead View of Dense Broiler Flock at Feeder Line
nodes.rationale: Ceiling-mounted colour CCTV still from a commercial broiler house, camera label '1080P-IPC-Siren', timestamp overlay 2022-03-14 22:13:57. Shows several hundred near-market-weight white broilers packed almost wall-to-wall on damp litter. A horizontal grey feed conveyor pipe crosses the frame with five red-capped circular pan feeders suspended from it; each pan holds visible feed and is ringed by birds head-in, producing the classic radial feeding cluster. Bird density is far higher and body size far larger than in the February frames, marking a late point in the grow-out cycle.

nodes.label: Overhead Broiler-House CCTV Surveillance Frame
nodes.rationale: All frames in this chunk share one acquisition modality: a fixed 1080p wide-angle IP camera mounted in the ceiling of a commercial broiler house, looking near-vertically down at the litter floor. The fixed viewpoint means background (feed line, walls, cables) is static across frames, so only the birds move — a property that makes simple background/foreground and density-based methods viable alongside detection models.

nodes.label: Suspended Pan Feeder Line
nodes.rationale: A horizontal conveyor pipe crossing every frame, carrying four to five circular pan feeders with red caps (colour frames) or pale grey grilles (infrared frames). It is the single most stable landmark in the scene and effectively defines the region of interest for feeding-behaviour analysis: bird positions are meaningful mainly relative to these fixed pan centres.

nodes.label: Feeding Cluster at Feeder Pan
nodes.rationale: The recurring behavioural unit visible from above: a compact ring of birds pressed against a pan with heads inward. Because the overhead view hides beaks and heads under the pan rim, the cluster geometry itself — not the head pose — is the observable cue that feeding is occurring.

nodes.label: Burned-In Timestamp and Camera Label Overlay
nodes.rationale: Every frame carries a top-right date-time string and a top-left camera identifier rendered by the DVR into the pixels. This gives free per-frame provenance (which camera, which moment, therefore which bird age and which light period) but also injects fixed high-contrast text that can be learned as a spurious feature or trigger false detections at the image border.

nodes.label: Camera 1080P-IPC-Siren
nodes.rationale: The dominant camera in this chunk, supplying frames 02101, 02501, 025501, 03201 and 03801 across both colour and infrared modes and across several weeks of the grow-out.

nodes.label: Broiler Growth-Stage Progression Across the Grow-Out Cycle
nodes.rationale: Timestamps run from 22 February to 14 March 2022 and apparent bird size grows correspondingly, from small scattered chicks to near-market broilers filling the frame. Sampling the whole cycle rather than one day means the detector must cope with object scale changing several-fold under a fixed camera, which is the main reason frames from different dates cannot be treated as interchangeable.

nodes.label: Stocking Density and Occlusion Severity
nodes.rationale: By the late frames birds touch and overlap almost everywhere, so individual outlines merge into continuous white mass. This caps the accuracy any per-bird bounding-box detector can reach late in the cycle and argues for density-estimation or region-level occupancy metrics as a complementary readout.

nodes.label: Frame Sampling for Behaviour-Detection Training Data
nodes.rationale: The img/ directory holds sparsely numbered stills (02101, 02501, 025501, 02701, 03201, 03801) decimated from continuous video. Sampling widely separated frames instead of consecutive ones maximises appearance diversity per annotation hour and avoids the near-duplicate redundancy that inflates apparent accuracy when consecutive video frames leak between train and validation splits.
